label: input q at original positions 2-4
explanation: Fires on every step where the input token is q at original-phase positions 2, 3 or 4 (dev precision 1.0, recall 0.999), and essentially never anywhere else. It does not fire on q at positions 0-1 or 5+, on any other token, or on the delimiter. In the copy phase it fires only on a trace of ~49 weak activations, when q is fed back at step 5 (recall_idx 2, i.e. L=3 sequences with q at original position 1). Magnitude depends on position: t=3 is strongest (top activations are all q at t=3, and t=3 carries 48% of mass from about the same number of steps as t=2), t=2 is intermediate, and t=4 is weakest (the lowest-quartile examples are q at t=4).

issues: No systematic gap found. Test: precision 1.0, recall 0.999, F1 0.9995, mass recall 0.99985, with 0 false positives.

The only misses are 43 test-split steps (49 on dev), all at t=5 in L=3 copy-phase sequences where q is fed back after being at original position 1. Activations are weak (0.04 to 0.19 of max) and hold 0.0% of the activation mass. This matches the explanation exactly.

The magnitude claims hold. t=3 alone covers 100% of the top activation quartile and 0% of the bottom two. t=4 covers 81% of the bottom quartile and 0% of the top. Mass per step ranks t=3 > t=2 > t=4 (0.478/16372 vs 0.305/16742 vs 0.217/13803).
Activation is zero at the delimiter, at t=0-1 and at t>=6. On dev, every activation is on input q and there are none on other tokens.
Minor wording point: the label says 'original positions 2-4', but there is weak, negligible firing on copy-phase q at t=5. The explanation already discloses this.
